title: db_domain's index door can declare a UNIQUE index: additive, owner-gated, never converting
intention: store.add_owned_index(table, owner, name, columns, *, unique=False) builds a UNIQUE index when unique=True: the owner alone may call it, a name that already stands as a non-unique index is never converted (SchemaChangeRefused), and building one over rows that hold a duplicate raises and leaves no index.
why: The librarian row-id migration (T5) gives 39 leaf tables a `row bigint` column. The row is the identity (Q#104, outline 4.3.1.5.1.6: node ids are master row numbers), so a duplicate row is a wrong-data read the database should refuse, not a convention. The ADD-COLUMN door takes a bare type and cannot carry UNIQUE by design, so the guarantee rides the index door, the one the store already has for an owner-gated index.
traces_to: Law 4 (identity enforced by the database, not by a caller), Law 6 (the owner alone gates its table's schema), Law 7 (a duplicate is refused loudly).
how: D1: a keyword `unique` on add_owned_index; CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS; before it, a pg_class/pg_index read of the name: standing with a different uniqueness raises SchemaChangeRefused (never a silent IF NOT EXISTS no-op that leaves a non-unique index where a unique one was asked for). A build over duplicate rows lets Postgres's own UniqueViolation raise (the statement is atomic: no index is left). NULLs stay distinct under a unique index, so a column still being filled is unconstrained until it is. D2: a proof, three teeth.

clauses.claim: the owner's unique index refuses a second row holding the same value, accepts distinct values, and asking again is a no-op; NULLs stay distinct
a non-owner is refused with OwnershipError and no index exists afterwards
a name standing as a non-unique index asked for as unique raises SchemaChangeRefused and stays non-unique; a unique build over rows holding a duplicate raises and leaves no index

decisions.text: D1: the unique keyword and the standing-index check in add_owned_index.
D2: the proof, one tooth per clause, over scratch tables the store drops at exit.

out: the ADD-COLUMN door (its own ticket, lands first)

measured.saw: add_owned_index builds CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and has no way to declare UNIQUE; a name already standing makes IF NOT EXISTS a silent no-op whatever uniqueness was asked
measured.how: read store.py add_owned_index on the add-column branch

measured.saw: after the build the three teeth read green on Windows and red unfixed (TypeError: unexpected keyword 'unique'); the existing index proof and the add-column proof still read green
UNMEASURED: that every one of the 39 leaf tables is free of duplicate row values at migration time (a duplicate makes the build raise, by design); T5's own measurement
